text:
OncallBot: :rotating_light: Paging: High latency spike on /v1/generate in us-east-1 — p95 jumped from ~220ms -> 1.8s; p99 ~3.6s. Auto-scaler still healthy. Paging oncall (maya).

Maya Patel: ack, looking. seeing increased queue depth on inference-runtime-01. pulling logs now. attaching tail of router logs:
```
router-01 | 2026-02-25T15:22:11Z INFO request-id=abc123 model=r2-large latency=362ms
router-01 | 2026-02-25T15:22:12Z WARN request-id=def456 queue-time=980ms batch-size=1
router-01 | 2026-02-25T15:22:15Z ERROR request-id=ghi789 backend=serving-03 grpc-code=14
```

Maya Patel: early sign this is not total capacity — looks like tail latency + some transient gRPC errors. checking KV cache hit rates.

Ashwin Kumar: I can see a spike in KV cache evictions around 15:20 UTC; likely a recent model rollout with larger KV footprint. Cache hit dropped from 93% -> 67% which explains p99 jumps.

Liam Chen: +1 on KV eviction hypothesis. Were there any recent model version pins/rollouts today?

Maya Patel: Yes — we rolled r2-large:v2 to serving-03 at 14:58 as a canary (small %). rollout notes said larger past-context memory. Might be related.

Sophia Rivera: customer impact check: our downstream monitoring shows ~12 customers had >2s responses between 15:20-15:38. No user-facing 5xx spike (errors ~0.5% -> 1.8%). So mostly latency, some retries. Putting incident severity as P2 for now.

Maya Patel: mitigation plan — 1) rollback canary for serving-03 OR 2) temporarily increase KV cache size on serving pool + increase GC timeout. I'm leaning rollback to be safe. Thoughts?

Ashwin Kumar: rollback is faster. I'll prep rollback but we should also add a dashboard panel for KV/cache hit and eviction rate in the postmortem dashboard.

Liam Chen: roll it back and watch metrics. Also we should mute noisy low-priority alerts that keep paging us while we stabilize (e.g., transient gRPC 14 warnings). Sophia, can you open a silence?

Sophia Rivera: opening 30m silence on non-5xx grpc warnings in us-east-1. Will note in alert manager. :white_check_mark:

Maya Patel: rolling back r2-large:v2 on serving-03 now. will post status in ~3 mins.

OncallBot: Deploy action: rollback r2-large:v2 from serving-03 initiated by maya — rollback id rb-20260225-01.

Maya Patel: rollback completed, routing back to r2-large:v1. preliminary p95 down to ~260ms after 90s. p99 trending back down but still noisy.

Ashwin Kumar: confirming KV cache hit returned to ~91% after rollback. eviction rate dropped. Looks like root cause likely the new model's KV footprint + under-provisioned cache on that pool.

Liam Chen: good, can we capture all these signals into a dedicated incident-retro grafana dashboard so next time oncall can eyeball golden signals quickly? I'm thinking a dashboard with:
- p50/p95/p99 request latency (per-route)
- request rate & saturation (concurrency, queue length)
- GPU/CPU util + memory (per serving node)
- KV cache hit %, eviction rate, cache size over time
- batch-size distribution histogram
- gRPC error codes (by code) and percent change
- rollout events timeline (deploy IDs) with annotations to correlate
- customer impact panel (count of affected API keys) with link to owner
- drilldown to traces (tempo/span links)

Sophia Rivera: +1. Also add an alert-noise panel: number of distinct alerts firing over time to help tuning.

Maya Patel: agreed. For immediate followups:
- Ashwin: own the dashboard panels for KV and batch histograms (PR target EOD).
- Liam: own the latency panels and deploy annotation integration.
- Sophia: own alert tuning changes (threshold proposals + silence rules) and create a small runbook note for this class of rollout.
- Maya: write up short incident summary and coordinate postmortem.

GrafanaBot: Created dashboard draft "IRT Incident Retro - 2026-02-25" (id: 1387) in folder "Incidents/Retrospectives". URL: https://grafana.internal/d/1387/irt-incident-retro-2026-02-25

Maya Patel: opening a PR for dashboard edits now — link: https://git.internal/redwood/grafana-dashboards/pull/823. PR includes placeholder panels and queries for p95/p99.

Ashwin Kumar: adding initial queries for KV cache hit panel. Example PromQL I'm adding:
```
sum by(instance) (rate(kv_cache_evictions_total[1m])) / sum by(instance) (kv_cache_size_bytes)
```
Will refine to percent hit once I cleanse metrics.

Liam Chen: for latency panels I'll include 50/95/99 percentiles and a derivative for tail slope. Query example: `histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))`

Sophia Rivera: alert tuning proposals:
- p95 > 1s for 5m (major) -> keep as paged but add a 3m grace before paging
- p99 > 2.5s for 3m -> paged for critical services only (model-serving-prod route)
- grpc warning spike (non-5xx) -> alert to channel only, don't page unless accompanied by error-rate increase
I'll post the exact Alertmanager rule diffs in the PR: https://git.internal/redwood/alerting/pull/411

Maya Patel: also adding a panel that shows "recent rollouts" by scraping deploy logs and annotating the times. That will help correlation.

Liam Chen: important: add drilldown links on each panel to Tempo traces and to the runbook entry for rollout-induced(KV) issues. Drilldown should include `trace_id` in the query when available.

GrafanaBot: Panel 4 (Latency - p99) updated with drilldown link to Tempo.

Sophia Rivera: small note for postmortem: customer impact summary (for Postmortem doc):
- window: 15:20 - 15:38 UTC
- affected customers: ~12 (top 3 account IDs: acct-112, acct-774, acct-991)
- symptom: increased latency (p95 up to ~1.8s), small error spike
- mitigation: rollback of r2-large:v2 on serving-03 at 15:23 UTC -> metrics recovered by 15:24:50 UTC

Ashwin Kumar: starting dashboard PR now: https://git.internal/redwood/grafana-dashboards/pull/824 (panels: KV hit, eviction rate, batch histogram, per-instance GPU util). Please review.

Maya Patel: status check — do we need to keep the temporary alert silence beyond the 30m? Sophia?

Sophia Rivera: I'll leave it for 30m and then re-evaluate once all alerts are stable. If thresholds need permanent change, I'll open a rule change PR after the postmortem.

Liam Chen: handoff — I need to step into a meeting in 12 mins. Maya, can you hand me any outstanding context?

Maya Patel: handing to Liam. Key things: rollback id rb-20260225-01, watch for any re-rollouts, dashboard PRs (823,824) live, Ashwin owns KV panels, Sophia owns alert PR 411. If anything spikes again, page as P1. I'm logging this in incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/INC-20260225-07

Liam Chen: thanks — I have it. I'll keep monitoring til 16:00 UTC then formal postmortem tomorrow.

OncallBot: Incident status changed to: stabilized. Severity downgraded to P3 at 15:40 UTC.

Maya Patel: quick retro note: for future rollouts of memory-hungry models, add a pre-rollout checklist item to validate KV footprint against pool cache sizes and add automated canary traffic that exercises long-context paths.

Sophia Rivera: adding that checklist item to runbook (PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/pull/59).

Liam Chen: closing handoff — I'll follow up on the Grafana drilldowns and postmortem doc. Thanks everyone. :heart:
